profile.headline: Software Engineer at Kin Insurance
profile.summary:
I'm a maker at heart. My whole life has been spent fiddling, crafting, and building anything I could get my hands on. An avid knitter, I now often relate the problem-solving skills I learned from knitting to the problem-solving challenges involved in programming. (The key? Error Messages! Knitting doesn't have them - programming does. Therefore, I propose that knitting is more difficult!)

As a programmer, I've come to realize something about myself: I don't really care about the language or libraries I'm working in, as long as they get the job done. I learn by doing and by watching, and I love asking questions and sharing new things I've learned with others. As a result, I'm an active teacher and mentor for beginning students at DBC and through Chicago MeetUps.

As a team member, I'm a listener and prefer to hear people out before expressing my opinions - and I've learned to never be married to my code. If there's a better solution, I'd rather use it, I want it to be the best my team and I could do. I tend to rely on logic and results when coding, but I always want my team to feel proud and happy with the work we've done.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
* Implemented full stack solution enabling teachers to upload industry standard formatting. This involved building containerized, scalable micro-services in Python and Ruby utilizing AWS SQS, S3, and ECS with an EmberJS front-end.
* Worked with project managers, developers and support team to resolve time-sensitive technical issues.
* Stepped in as stand in project manager. Helped resolve issues with JIRA Workflow.
* Implemented gRPC Gateways for interop between Legacy Monolith application and microservices
* Extensively interfaced with legacy perl code

positions.title: Junior Software Engineer
positions.description:
* At Opternative, an online eye refraction solution, I worked extensively with Ruby on Rails, AngularJS, PostgreSQL, a bit of ReactJS, CSS and Sass.
* As a full stack engineer I had a hand in a design overhaul, as well as ReactJS working with our eye refraction algorithms.

positions.title: Private Tutor
positions.description: Private Tutor for students learning the fundamentals of Object Oriented Programming, with a focus on Ruby, Rails and JavaScript.  Emphasis on recognizing one's learning process, methods for problem-solving, and enjoying the challenges of programming.

positions.title: Personal Development - Web Developer
positions.description: Post graduate self-study and building of random fun apps.

positions.title: Software Development Student
positions.description:
Dev Bootcamp is a 19-week intensive training program for aspiring web developers, specializing in Ruby, Rails, HTML5, CSS, Test Driven Development, Object-Oriented Javascript (AJAX, JQuery), Git and Source Control, Heroku, and Agile Development. I graduated from the program in June 2014.

The first 9 weeks of the curriculum are remote, while the second 9 weeks are an immersive in-class experience. The program also addresses intra- and interpersonal strategies for fostering optimal learning and teamwork environments.

The program culminates with an 8-day final project, where we pitch, design, and develop an application over the course of a week. I worked with the team that built Polity, an app built with Ruby on Rails, HTML, and CSS to connect Chicagoans with their local alderman in order to see how they are voting.

volunteerExperiences.description: I assisted budding programmers with the RailsBridge Curriculum. Some of my main responsibilities were teaching the basics of MVC architecture, Rails routing and, my favorite, ActiveRecord associations. I also taught how to effectively troubleshoot and identify issues.
Mentoring Dev Bootcamp students with Ruby, HTML/CSS, Javascript, and Rails.

projects.title: Read Herring
projects.description:
Hey YOU! Read a BOOK! Keep track of the books you need to read because your friends learned to read at a young age and now tell you all the good books that you can't (or won't) keep track of!

Purpose
This is my first real forray into EmberJS. Currently learning with a friend who was sent to EmberJS Training Camp, we decided a nice small project that wasn't a damn TODO app was good to express the power of EmberJS. Also, we intend to use Bourbon instead of Foundation or Bootstrap as our front-end framework, because I haven't played with it much, and because it's light.

Execution
* Ember CLI (for full MVC)
* Bourbon front-end framework (because it's nice and light)
* OpenLibrary's API (for book information)
* Data Storage is still up in the air :)
* Also would like to practice some real web design - meaning, Photoshop!
  * I intend to draw up Photoshop Mock-Ups
  * Learn how to build a Photoshop Asset Library
  * Use Photoshop Asset Linking
  * Design for front-end frameworks like Foundation's Columns and Grid system

projects.title: Roam v.2 - The Tummy Tuck and Facelift
projects.description:
In my current iteration, I'm using a number of JavaScript libraries I've spent time learning.  More than a simle facelift, I decided a while ago to get over my lack of interest in the Front End - especially since the lines between front-end and back-end are getting more blurred every day.

Purpose
* Pick a few of my favorite Javascript Libraries from a seemingly endless JS flavors-of-the-month.
* Employ clean, purpose-built code for speed and legitibility.

Execution
* LeafletJS for mapping
* EmberJS for MVC/Frontend
* Ruby On Rails w/ Grape for building APIs and backend heavy-lifting and non-user-facing functionality
